prompt.difference: Merge two numbers that are {target} apart.
prompt.bundleTen: Merge ones to make a ten.
prompt.bundleHundred: Merge ones into tens, and tens into a hundred.
prompt.fraction: Merge parts to make one whole.
prompt.doubleFact: Merge two numbers that are the same.
prompt.double: Merge the same numbers to double them. Make {target}.

wrong.title: Not a pair
wrong.notSame: {a} and {b} are not the same. Find two {a}s.

refuse.notFactor: {a} × {b} = {value}. {target} is not in the {value} times table, so you could not reach it.
refuse.overTen: {a} and {b} ones are more than one ten. Make exactly 10.
refuse.overHundred: {a} and {b} make more than 100. Make exactly 100.
refuse.mixed: Ones merge with ones, and tens merge with tens.
refuse.far: Move a tile onto a tile right next to it.

status.reshuffled: No moves were left, so new tiles fell in.
status.dragOrTap: Drag a number onto the one next to it, or tap one and then the other.
status.tapOnly: Tap a number, then tap the one next to it.

hint.bond: {a} needs {need} to make {target}. Look for a {need} next to it.
hint.difference: {target} apart means the bigger one is {target} more. Look for {a} and {need} side by side.
hint.build: You need exactly {target}. Merge small tiles first, then finish with the right one.
hint.product: Think of the {target} times facts. Merge two numbers that multiply to a part of {target}.
hint.bundle: Ones go with ones and tens go with tens. Stop at exactly 10 or 100.
hint.fraction: Add the parts. Stop when the top and bottom numbers are the same.
hint.doubleFact: Look for two tiles with the same number, side by side.
hint.double: Only the same numbers merge. Make two the same, then merge them to double.
hint.worked: Move the {a} onto the {b} next to it.

method.bond: Think of the partner: what do you add to make {target}?
method.difference: Count on from the smaller number to find the bigger one.
method.doubleFact: Double means the same number twice: add it to itself.
method.double: Double means the same number twice: add it to itself.
method.sum: Add the numbers you have, then count on to {target}.
method.product: Use the times facts: which number times this one makes {target}?
method.bundle: Ten ones make one ten, and ten tens make one hundred.
method.fraction: Count the parts you have, then the parts still missing from one whole.
